audit_findings.title: Post-acquisition numerator and denominator describe different businesses
audit_findings.magnitude: 38.542 million acquisition shares; valuation denominator 99.562111 million versus 60.075 million pre-close fully diluted shares (+65.7% computed); denominator-only base value would be $164.68 per share versus $99.36, with omitted BDS owner earnings unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Legacy-only owner earnings are divided by post-close shares while post-close cash is used in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The 2025 financial results of the BDS Business are not included in the Company’s 2025 consolidated financial results presented herein.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter error, not merely a possible issue. The filing confirms that 2025 results exclude BDS while the valuation includes the acquisition shares. Correcting only the denominator would materially increase every per-share result, although $164.68 remains below the $409.38 market price. Because normalized BDS owner earnings are also missing, the combined-company valuation conclusion remains unestablished.
audit_findings.action: Rerun on one consistent perimeter: either derive normalized combined-company owner earnings using post-close filings, 99.562111 million shares and the post-close bridge, or use 60.075 million legacy fully diluted shares with the legacy balance sheet.

audit_findings.title: Interest on the newly assumed $4 billion debt is absent from the owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: 2026 first-half interest expense $108 million versus $28 million in the prior-year period, a filed $80 million increase; computed annual coupons on the $3.5 billion fixed-rate acquisition notes are approximately $165.8 million, or 24.9% of the $665.7 million anchor, before the variable-rate term loan and tax effects
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring after-tax acquisition financing costs reduce equity-level owner earnings because this DCF retains interest expense rather than deducting debt principal in the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon consummation of the BDS Business Acquisition, the Company assumed $4.0 billion of indebtedness incurred by SpinCo in connection with the payment of the SpinCo Cash Distribution which consists of a $3.5 billion tranche maturing and payable in full on February 6, 2027 and a $500 million tranche maturing and payable in full on February 6, 2028.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated: a 2016–2025 anchor cannot contain debt interest first incurred in 2026. The filed increase and fixed coupons are large relative to the anchor. BDS earnings must also be added, but that does not cure omission of the associated financing cost.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile normalized combined owner earnings to the $108 million first-half interest expense, the five fixed-note coupons, the $450 million variable-rate term loan, revolving borrowings, debt-fee amortization, hedge settlements and the applicable tax benefit; rerun the DCF with recurring after-tax interest included.

audit_findings.title: The post-close liability perimeter has not been fully reconciled
audit_findings.magnitude: Purchase accounting identifies $197 million of other current and non-current liabilities and $1.637 billion of deferred tax liabilities; the independently bridge-deductible or cash-consuming subset is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Debt-like, contingent or incremental cash liabilities omitted from both normalized owner earnings and the equity bridge would reduce value attributable to common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: The BDS Business Acquisition involved numerous operational, strategic, financial, accounting, legal, tax and other risks, including potential liabilities associated with the integrated businesses.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing supplies preliminary liability balances, but it does not establish which items are ordinary operating liabilities already captured through earnings and working capital, which represent future tax cash flows, and which require a separate equity-bridge deduction. The $197 million other-liability balance is about 2.0% of the $9.893 billion base equity value, while the much larger deferred-tax balance is not automatically deductible dollar-for-dollar. Materiality therefore remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Map every provisional acquisition liability—including the $197 million other liabilities and $1.637 billion deferred-tax liability—to operating cash flow, owner-earnings adjustments or the bridge; obtain the final purchase-price allocation and rerun for any net debt-like or contingent claims not otherwise captured.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition and integration costs may be normalized inconsistently
audit_findings.magnitude: $97 million filed for 2025, equal to 14.6% of the $665.7 million anchor; 2026 first-half filings additionally report $121 million of transaction, integration and other internal costs, $52 million of restructuring charges and $40 million of TSA costs
audit_findings.mechanism: Removing genuinely nonrecurring costs raises normalized owner earnings, while omitting continuing integration, restructuring, TSA or financing costs overstates near-term owner earnings.
audit_findings.evidence: In addition, in connection with the acquisition of the BDS Business, the Company has incurred approximately $ 97 million of transaction, integration, financing and other internal costs for the year ended December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The cost amounts are demonstrated and large enough to affect normalized earning power, but their proper treatment is unresolved because the disclosures combine transaction, integration, financing and internal costs with different durations. Retaining every 2025 cost may understate sustainable earnings; projecting none of the continuing post-close costs would overstate them.
audit_findings.action: Trace each cost category through the 2025 owner-earnings series and 2026 results; document cash versus noncash treatment and expected duration, then rerun using only transaction costs proven nonrecurring while retaining integration, restructuring, TSA and financing costs for their supported periods.

audit_findings.title: Reverse Morris Trust tax indemnity is an unmodeled contingent claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A triggered indemnity would be a cash claim ahead of common equity, while the two-year restrictions could constrain repurchases, issuances or combinations relevant to growth and capital allocation.
audit_findings.evidence: If the Company or SpinCo take or omit to take any actions enumerated in the Tax Matters Agreement, or if certain events relating to SpinCo occur that would cause the Spin-Off or the SpinCo Cash Distribution to become taxable, the party whose actions or omissions (or event relating to) caused the Spin-Off or the SpinCo Cash Distribution to become taxable generally will be required to bear the cost of any resulting tax liability of BD (but not BD’s shareholders).
audit_findings.explanation: The agreement and potential liability are demonstrated, but the supplied record shows no triggering event, probability estimate, maximum exposure or recognized liability. This is therefore a forward-looking contingency rather than a presently demonstrated valuation error. The company states that taxes would be expected to be material if triggered.
audit_findings.action: Monitor Tax Matters Agreement compliance through February 2028; obtain the estimated BD tax exposure, triggering-event analysis, recognized contingency, insurance and indemnification offsets, and rerun the bridge or cash flows if an obligation becomes probable or measurable.

audit_findings.title: Unidentified D&A is conservatively left in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: identified eligible add-backs were $41.8 million in 2019 and $52.1 million in 2022; the residual composite D&A computes to approximately $63.5 million and $78.5 million, respectively, but the eligible portion is unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any residual depreciation or amortization proven to be a non-economic eligible add-back would increase historical owner earnings, the fitted trend and potentially the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: identified eligible D&A is below the filed composite; residual is conservatively left as an expense, not added back: FY2019 $41.8m (39.7% of filed D&A); FY2022 $52.1m (39.9% of filed D&A)
audit_findings.explanation: There is no demonstrated overstatement because unidentified D&A remains expensed. However, the residual pools equal approximately 12.8% of 2019 owner earnings and 12.3% of 2022 owner earnings, so the record cannot establish that the possible understatement is immaterial. Their economic eligibility remains unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Obtain filed D&A schedules by asset and expense category, reconcile them to maintenance capital expenditure and purchased-intangible treatment, and rerun the historical series and trend only for residual amounts supported as eligible non-economic add-backs.
